findings.title: No API interface — direct database access only
findings.description: The application exposes no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. It is a standalone VB6 desktop application that connects directly to a Microsoft Access .mdb file on a shared network drive via ADODB/Jet OLEDB. Integration requires direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No API layer exists. Agent integration would require either direct database manipulation (brittle, non-auditable) or UI automation (fragile, unscalable).
findings.recommendation: Create a thin REST API layer in front of the Access database to expose customer CRUD operations as HTTP endpoints.

findings.title: No machine identity authentication
findings.description: The application has no authentication mechanism. It relies entirely on the Windows username (Environ("USERNAME")) for identity attribution and Windows SMB file share permissions for access control. No OAuth2, API key, mTLS, or any machine identity support exists.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. An agent cannot authenticate to this system with attribution.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a service layer with OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication.

findings.title: No audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No audit logging exists. Errors are swallowed with On Error Resume Next and shown to users via MsgBox only. There is no CloudTrail, no structured logging, no log storage, and no immutable log configuration. Write operations (INSERT into Customers) are completely unaudited.
findings.gap: No audit trail for any operation. Agent-initiated writes cannot be attributed, traced, or forensically reviewed.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging for all write operations with immutable storage (CloudTrail + S3 Object Lock).

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application does not expose a documented REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. It is a legacy ColdFusion 8 server-rendered web application with two .cfm pages accessed via browser HTTP requests. Integration would require direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No API layer exists. The only integration surface is server-rendered HTML pages or direct SQL Server database access.
findings.recommendation: Define a REST API layer with OpenAPI documentation for document search and download functionality.

findings.title: No Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: Write operations have no idempotency controls. No idempotency keys, no unique constraints, no deduplication logic.
findings.gap: No idempotency key support. Duplicate agent calls would create duplicate records.
findings.recommendation: Add idempotency key support to all write endpoints with unique constraint enforcement.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses only session-based browser authentication. No OAuth2 client credentials, no API key authentication, no mTLS, no service accounts.
findings.gap: No machine identity mechanism. Agents cannot authenticate without browser-based session cookies.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key or OAuth2 client credentials flow for machine-to-machine authentication.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind. No CloudTrail, no application-level logging, no immutable storage. The application does not log who performed what action.
findings.gap: No audit trail. Cannot prove compliance or conduct forensics.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging with principal attribution stored in append-only storage.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanisms. No sagas, no undo endpoints, no transactional boundaries. Write operations are immediate and irreversible.
findings.gap: Failed multi-step operations leave partial state with no recovery mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Implement transactional boundaries with rollback support for write operations.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application serves HTML pages via Django views (ticket_list, ticket_search). No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Integration requires UI automation or direct database access.
findings.gap: No programmatic API interface exists. Only HTML-based web views or direct PostgreSQL access.
findings.recommendation: Build REST API with Django REST Framework after upgrading Python/Django to supported versions.

findings.title: Write Operations Not Idempotent
findings.description: Django admin provides CRUD operations with no idempotency key support. No idempotency middleware or unique constraint enforcement on business keys.
findings.gap: Write operations are not idempotent. Agent retries would create duplicate records.
findings.recommendation: Implement idempotency keys on all write endpoints when building the REST API.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Only Django session-based authentication. No OAuth2 client credentials, API keys, mTLS, or service account support.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism. Agents cannot authenticate with attributable identities.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication for machine callers.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. No CloudTrail, no application-level audit trail, no immutable log storage. Only a print statement logging search queries.
findings.gap: No authenticated principal attribution on operations. No immutable audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging (CloudTrail + S3 Object Lock) with principal identity for every operation.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposed Without Scoping
findings.description: Stage A: System stores user PII (requester names, ticket content). Stage B/B1: ticket_list returns requester data without field filtering. No serializers or DTOs. B2: No access control differentiation. B3: No classification metadata.
findings.gap: Agent-facing responses include all sensitive fields without scoping.
findings.recommendation: Implement response serializers excluding sensitive fields. Create separate agent-facing DTOs with OAuth scope differentiation.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: User PII stored on single EC2 with no data residency documentation, region configuration, or controls preventing cross-region transmission.
findings.gap: No data residency policy or technical enforcement. Agent could transmit data cross-jurisdiction.
findings.recommendation: Document residency requirements. Implement region-locked controls for data transmission.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Capability
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanisms. No saga patterns, compensating transactions, or undo endpoints.
findings.gap: Failed multi-step workflows leave application in partial state.
findings.recommendation: Implement transaction boundaries and compensation endpoints for multi-step workflows.

findings.title: No Machine-Consumable API — Form-Based HTML Only
findings.description: The application exposes only a Struts 1.3 HTML form-based interface mapped to /loan via struts-config.xml. There is no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration requires UI automation or direct database access.
findings.gap: No machine-consumable API exists. The only integration surface is a Struts Action that renders JSP pages.
findings.recommendation: Create a REST API layer (e.g., Spring Boot or JAX-RS) exposing loan calculation and submission as JSON endpoints.

findings.title: Non-Idempotent Write Operations — Duplicate Records on Retry
findings.description: The saveApplication() method performs a plain SQL INSERT with no idempotency key, no unique constraint on business keys, and no deduplication logic. Repeated calls create duplicate loan application records.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism exists. Agent retries or LLM non-determinism would create duplicate loan applications.
findings.recommendation: Add a unique business key and enforce with database UNIQUE constraint. Accept idempotency keys in requests.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication — Container-Managed Only
findings.description: The application relies exclusively on container-managed authentication via request.getRemoteUser() (WebLogic security realm). No OAuth2 client credentials, no API keys, no mTLS, no service accounts.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism. Agents cannot authenticate as distinct principals.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication with principal attribution.

findings.title: No Audit Logging — Zero Traceability for Write Operations
findings.description: No logging exists in the application — no logging framework, no log statements, no audit trail. Write operations cannot be traced, attributed, or forensically reviewed.
findings.gap: Zero audit logging infrastructure. Agent-initiated write operations are untraceable.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging with principal attribution and immutable storage.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Unscoped — PII and Financial Data Flow Without Filtering
findings.description: System stores PII (applicant names) and financial data (loan details). No field-level filtering, no response DTOs, no access differentiation. Single database credential provides full access.
findings.gap: B1: Sensitive data flows unfiltered through all layers. B2: Single-credential access with no differentiation.
findings.recommendation: Implement response DTOs excluding sensitive fields; create separate OAuth scopes for PII access.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls for Financial PII
findings.description: Financial PII stored in Oracle 11g with no documented residency controls. No policies preventing cross-jurisdiction data transmission by agents.
findings.gap: Financial PII without residency controls. Agent could transmit regulated data cross-region.
findings.recommendation: Document residency requirements; enforce at the API boundary.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback for Write Operations
findings.description: The saveApplication() method performs a single INSERT with no compensation, undo, or rollback capability. No saga patterns, no undo endpoints, no compensating transactions.
findings.gap: No compensation mechanism. Failed multi-step workflows leave partial state.
findings.recommendation: Implement status-based lifecycle (PENDING → CONFIRMED → CANCELLED) for reversibility.

findings.title: No Agent-Consumable API Interface
findings.description: The application exposes a SOAP 1.1 RPC/encoded endpoint defined by a hand-maintained WSDL that drifts from implementation. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Modern agent frameworks cannot bind to SOAP/WSDL natively.
findings.gap: No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. SOAP RPC/encoded is deprecated and not consumable by agent tool frameworks.
findings.recommendation: Create a REST API wrapper (e.g., Spring Boot @RestController) exposing POST /orders with JSON request/response and auto-generated OpenAPI specification.

findings.title: Non-Idempotent Write Endpoint
findings.description: The submitOrder endpoint performs INSERT INTO partner_orders with no idempotency key, no duplicate detection, and no unique constraint enforcement. Same request creates duplicate records.
findings.gap: No idempotency key support, no unique constraint on (partner_id, po_number), no deduplication logic.
findings.recommendation: Add UNIQUE constraint on (partner_id, po_number) and implement idempotency key support in the replacement API.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists in the codebase. README mentions WS-Security username token (plaintext) but no implementation is present. No OAuth2, API keys, or mTLS.
findings.gap: No agent-attributable machine identity mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials flow or API key authentication with principal attribution.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind. No logging framework, no CloudTrail, no write-operation attribution. Cannot determine who initiated operations.
findings.gap: No audit trail for agent write operations. Cannot prove compliance or conduct forensics.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging with immutable storage (CloudTrail or S3 Object Lock).

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposed in Error Responses
findings.description: Stage A: YES — partner financial data and hardcoded DB credentials. B1: Raw exception messages expose DB connection strings and infrastructure details to callers. B2: No access control differentiation. B3: No classification metadata.
findings.gap: B1: Raw exceptions expose DB details. B2: Single shared credential for all callers. B3: No classification.
findings.recommendation: Immediately sanitize error responses. Implement access differentiation. Add data classification tags.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: Partner financial transaction data stored with no residency documentation, no region-specific configuration, no sovereignty controls.
findings.gap: No jurisdictional classification for financial transaction data. Cannot assess compliance risk for agent LLM transmission.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements. Classify whether data falls under GDPR, LGPD, PCI-DSS.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback
findings.description: Immediate INSERT with no compensation or rollback capability. No saga pattern, no undo endpoint, no compensating transactions.
findings.gap: Cannot reverse agent-initiated writes. Failed multi-step workflows leave partial state.
findings.recommendation: Add order status lifecycle (PENDING → CONFIRMED → CANCELLED) with cancel/void endpoint.

findings.title: No API Interface — Batch File Exchange Only
findings.description: The system has no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. It is a COBOL batch program orchestrated by JCL, exchanging data via fixed-width flat files transmitted over plaintext FTP to an EC2 gateway at 10.0.7.40.
findings.gap: No API layer exists. Integration requires file-based exchange or mainframe job submission.
findings.recommendation: Expose the payroll calculation logic behind a REST API or wrap the batch job trigger as an API endpoint.

findings.title: Non-Idempotent Batch Execution
findings.description: The batch job is not idempotent. Running PAYRUN twice for the same pay period produces duplicate output records. No idempotency key, no deduplication, no duplicate detection mechanism.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism. Duplicate job submission results in duplicate payroll output.
findings.recommendation: Add a pay-period identifier check at job start that detects and rejects duplicate runs.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: No machine identity authentication exists. The only credential is a hardcoded FTP username/password in the JCL. No mechanism to identify which agent or service triggered the batch job.
findings.gap: No machine identity infrastructure. Cannot authenticate callers or attribute actions to specific principals.
findings.recommendation: Implement service account authentication for job submission with principal attribution.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. Only JCL SYSOUT which is not immutable or tamper-evident. No record of authenticated principals for financial operations.
findings.gap: No immutable audit trail. SOX compliance exposure for payroll/financial operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging with principal attribution and tamper-evident storage.

findings.title: Unscoped Sensitive Data Access (SSN, Bank Accounts)
findings.description: System processes SSN (EMP-SSN), bank accounts (EMP-ACCT), pay rates, and net compensation with no field-level access scoping. All fields equally accessible with no filtering.
findings.gap: B1: No mechanism to exclude sensitive fields from data access. B2: No access differentiation between sensitive and non-sensitive data. B3: No data classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Implement field-level access controls separating SSN/bank account access from general payroll data.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls for Regulated PII
findings.description: US SSN and financial data transmitted via plaintext FTP with no residency controls, no encryption, no region constraints, and no documented compliance policy.
findings.gap: No data residency policy. No encryption in transit. Regulated PII transmitted without protection.
findings.recommendation: Document residency requirements, replace plaintext FTP with encrypted transfer, implement region-pinning.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Capability
findings.description: No compensation or rollback capability exists. Partial failures leave the system in indeterminate state. FTP step has no error handling.
findings.gap: No rollback, no compensation, no partial-failure recovery.
findings.recommendation: Add checkpoint/restart logic and error handling for multi-step batch execution.

findings.title: No structured API interface — CGI returns HTML
findings.description: The application exposes a CGI binary (pricing.cgi) via Apache httpd that accepts HTTP GET requests with query parameters sku and qty. The response is HTML (Content-Type: text/html) meant for human consumption, not a structured REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface.
findings.gap: No structured API interface exists. The only integration path is parsing HTML output from a CGI endpoint — fragile, non-auditable, and unsuitable for agent tool binding.
findings.recommendation: Replace CGI with a modern REST API returning JSON, or add a JSON response mode (Accept: application/json header or format=json parameter) returning structured pricing data.

findings.title: No machine identity authentication
findings.description: The application has no authentication mechanism. The CGI endpoint is accessible to any caller without credentials. No OAuth2, API keys, mTLS, or authorization headers are checked. The Kubernetes service exposes the endpoint on ClusterIP without any authentication layer.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication exists. Any caller can invoke the pricing endpoint without identification or attribution. Agent calls cannot be distinguished from other traffic.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway in front of the K8s service with API key authentication or OAuth2 client credentials. Require all callers to present a valid identity.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses a single hardcoded static API key (ship-2013-abc123-static) checked via x-api-key header middleware. There is no per-caller identity, no OAuth2 client credentials flow, no mTLS, and no principal attribution.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. A single shared secret provides no caller attribution — impossible to distinguish which agent or service made a request.
findings.recommendation: Replace the static shared API key with an API Gateway authorizer using per-caller API keys or OAuth2 client credentials. Each agent identity should receive a unique credential attributable in access logs.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application exposes a Rails 2.3 controller with implicit routes (index, create, show) but has no documented API interface. Integration requires reverse-engineering controller code.
findings.gap: No API documentation. Endpoints discoverable only via code inspection.
findings.recommendation: Document existing controller endpoints as an OpenAPI 3.0 specification. Add explicit REST API layer with versioned routes.

findings.title: No Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: POST /orders has no idempotency key support. Retries create duplicate orders and trigger duplicate payment charges to the SOAP gateway.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism on write endpoints. Duplicate requests create duplicate records and charges.
findings.recommendation: Add idempotency key parameter with server-side deduplication and unique constraint enforcement.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: No authentication mechanism exists. Comment explicitly states missing before_filter for auth. Any caller can access any endpoint without identification.
findings.gap: Complete absence of authentication. No machine identity, no principal attribution.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials flow or API key authentication with per-caller principal attribution.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind. Write operations (order creation, payment charges) not logged with caller identity. No CloudTrail, no immutable log storage.
findings.gap: Complete absence of audit logging and immutable log storage.
findings.recommendation: Implement audit logging with CloudTrail and S3 Object Lock for immutable storage.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposed in API Responses
findings.description: Stage A: System processes PCI-regulated credit card data (card_number, card_exp). Stage B: B1 fires — Order.find returns all fields including card data with no filtering. B2 fires — no access differentiation exists.
findings.gap: B1: Card data exposed in API responses. B2: No access control differentiation. B3: No classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Add field filtering to exclude card_number/card_exp from API responses. Implement tokenized card storage.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls for PCI Data
findings.description: PCI-regulated payment card data stored in MySQL on EC2 with no residency controls, no region constraints, no data sovereignty policies.
findings.gap: No data residency policies for PCI data. No controls preventing cross-jurisdiction data transmission.
findings.recommendation: Implement region-locked storage with data sovereignty policies. Prevent card data from reaching LLM providers.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback
findings.description: Multi-step create+charge workflow has no compensation logic. Failed payment after order save leaves orphaned database record with no reversal mechanism.
findings.gap: No compensation or rollback for multi-step write operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement saga pattern with compensation logic for order-create-then-charge workflow.

findings.title: No Programmatic API — WebForms Only
findings.description: The application is a legacy ASP.NET WebForms app that renders server-side HTML pages. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Integration requires UI automation or direct database access.
findings.gap: No programmatic API. Only browser-rendered WebForms UI.
findings.recommendation: Build a REST API layer exposing timesheet read/write operations.

findings.title: Non-Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: INSERT operations have no idempotency key, no unique constraints, no duplicate detection. Repeated submissions create duplicate timesheet entries.
findings.gap: Non-idempotent writes — repeated submissions create duplicates.
findings.recommendation: Add idempotency keys and unique business-key constraints on (employee_id, entry_date, project).

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses ASP.NET Forms authentication with browser-based session cookies. No support for service account authentication, client credentials OAuth 2.0, API keys, or mTLS.
findings.gap: No machine identity mechanism. Authentication is exclusively human-interactive.
findings.recommendation: Introduce OAuth 2.0 client credentials or API key authentication for programmatic access with principal attribution.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind. Write operations have no principal attribution, no timestamp recording, no immutable log trail.
findings.gap: Complete absence of audit logging and immutable log storage.
findings.recommendation: Implement audit logging with principal attribution and immutable storage (CloudWatch Logs, S3 with object lock).

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback for Write Operations
findings.description: Direct SQL INSERT with no transaction management, no saga pattern, no compensation logic, and no undo endpoints. Once inserted, entries cannot be reversed.
findings.gap: No compensation or rollback capability. INSERT operations immediately committed.
findings.recommendation: Implement SQL transactions and soft-delete/status lifecycle for reversal capability.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: The application does not log the authenticated principal for write operations. The deleteProduct and upsertProduct mutations execute without recording who performed the action. The code explicitly acknowledges this gap. No CloudTrail configuration exists in the IaC, and no application-level audit logging is present.
findings.gap: No immutable, tamper-evident audit log correlating the authenticated principal (JWT sub claim) with each write operation.
findings.recommendation: Add structured audit event emission in mutation resolvers — extract sub and client_id from JWT claims and emit a JSON log entry with {principal, action, sku, timestamp} to CloudWatch Logs with retention policy.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: Write endpoints (POST /orders, DELETE /orders/{id}, POST /orders/{id}/refund, POST /orders/{id}/cancel) have no idempotency key support. The code explicitly documents: 'No Idempotency-Key => a retry double-refunds.'
findings.gap: No idempotency middleware, no Idempotency-Key header support, no unique constraint enforcement on business keys for write operations.
findings.recommendation: Add Idempotency-Key header support to all state-mutating endpoints using a Fastify plugin that stores idempotency keys in PostgreSQL.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: The ECS task definition configures CloudWatch logging (awslogs driver) but the application does not log the authenticated principal (JWT subject/roles) for write operations. No CloudTrail configuration exists. CloudWatch Logs are not configured with immutability controls.
findings.gap: Authenticated principal not logged per write operation. No immutable/tamper-evident log storage. No CloudTrail.
findings.recommendation: Attach JWT sub claim to Fastify request context in auth middleware; configure structured logging to include principal. Export logs to S3 with Object Lock.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The system stores customer-identifiable data (customerId, order transaction amounts) in PostgreSQL. No data residency documentation, sovereignty policies, or cross-boundary transfer restrictions exist.
findings.gap: No data residency policy documented. No boundary controls restricting data transmission to specific regions or jurisdictions.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements for customer order data. Identify applicable regulations based on customer base geography. Add data classification tags to infrastructure resources.

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: Multi-step write operations (refund: update DB + call payment; cancel: update DB + call warehouse) perform sequential mutations without compensation logic. If downstream call fails after DB update, system is left in inconsistent state.
findings.gap: No saga pattern, no compensating transactions, no atomic multi-step execution.
findings.recommendation: Wrap multi-step operations in database transactions; commit only after downstream success, or implement compensating actions.

findings.title: No Idempotency on Write Operations
findings.description: Write endpoints (POST /api/orders, POST /api/returns, etc.) do not support idempotency keys. Each POST creates a new record unconditionally using uniqid() for IDs.
findings.gap: No idempotency key support, no deduplication mechanism. Duplicate requests create duplicate records.
findings.recommendation: Implement Idempotency-Key header support with server-side deduplication table and TTL.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses PHP session-based authentication with cookie-based login. No OAuth2 client credentials flow, no API key authentication with principal attribution, no mTLS, and no service account mechanism exists.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism. The only auth path is human-oriented session login.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials flow or API key authentication with per-agent identity attribution for programmatic callers.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: The application logs order status changes to a mutable MySQL table (order_status_history). No CloudTrail configuration, no immutable log storage (S3 Object Lock), no tamper-evident audit trail.
findings.gap: No immutable audit trail for write operations. Existing logs can be modified or deleted.
findings.recommendation: Enable CloudTrail with log file validation and configure S3 bucket with Object Lock for immutable audit storage.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: The system stores customer PII (names, emails, addresses) in MySQL/RDS with no data residency policies, region restrictions, or compliance framework references. No controls prevent cross-region data transmission.
findings.gap: No data residency configuration, no compliance documentation, no controls for cross-boundary data transmission.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements, add region constraints to IaC, implement controls preventing cross-boundary data transmission to LLM providers.

findings.title: No Compensation/Rollback for Multi-Step Workflows
findings.description: The fulfillment workflow (validate → assign-warehouse → pick → pack → quality-check → ship) has no saga pattern or compensation logic. Each step commits independently with no undo mechanism.
findings.gap: No compensation or rollback for multi-step workflows. Partial failures leave the system in an inconsistent state.
findings.recommendation: Implement compensating actions for each workflow step or adopt a saga pattern with explicit rollback states.

findings.title: No scoped permissions — single shared database password
findings.description: No authorization model exists. The application uses a single shared database password for all users. All users have identical full read/write access to the entire database.
findings.gap: No scoped permissions mechanism. Cannot grant an agent read-only access to specific resources.
findings.recommendation: Implement role-based scoped permissions in the new API layer.

findings.title: No action-level authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. Any user who can access the .mdb file can execute any SQL operation on any table. No ABAC, RBAC, or middleware enforcing action-level restrictions.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to read-only operations on a specific resource type.
findings.recommendation: Build fine-grained RBAC with action-level authorization into the new service layer.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in source code
findings.description: Database credentials are hardcoded as plaintext constants in source code (Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw"). The credential is committed to the git repository and compiled into the distributed EXE.
findings.gap: Hardcoded credentials in source code. No secrets management, no rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Migrate credential storage to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation. Remove hardcoded credentials from source code and git history.

findings.title: No agent identity suspension mechanism
findings.description: No identity management exists. Since there are no agent identities, API keys, or service accounts, there is no mechanism to suspend or revoke a specific agent's access without affecting all users.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without disrupting all users.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent API keys with individual revocation when building the API layer.

findings.title: Customer PII stored without access scoping or differentiation
findings.description: Stage A: Yes — the system stores customer PII (names) and user identifiers. Stage B: B1 — No API exists for response scoping (RISK-SAFETY due to surface-flag downgrade from BLOCKER). B2 — No access differentiation (RISK-SAFETY). B3 — No classification metadata (INFO). Overall: RISK-SAFETY.
findings.gap: No API response scoping, no access control differentiation, no classification metadata for customer PII.
findings.recommendation: Build API response DTOs with field-level filtering and differentiated access scopes for agent vs internal consumers.

findings.title: No input validation — SQL injection vulnerability
findings.description: Zero input validation. User input from txtName.Text is directly concatenated into SQL strings without any validation, sanitization, or parameterization. This creates a SQL injection vulnerability.
findings.gap: No input validation. SQL injection risk. No structured validation error responses.
findings.recommendation: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized queries. Implement input validation with structured error responses.

findings.title: No schema documentation or versioning
findings.description: No schema documentation, no API contracts, no versioning exists. The database schema is implicit (inferred from SQL statements only). No migration files, no schema registry, no changelog.
findings.gap: No documented or versioned schema. Agent tool bindings would have no stable contract to bind against.
findings.recommendation: Document the database schema and implement API versioning in the new service layer.

findings.title: Zero test coverage
findings.description: No tests exist. README explicitly states 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine.' No test files, no test frameworks, no test infrastructure.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage for any functionality.
findings.recommendation: Build comprehensive API test suites (integration tests, contract tests) as part of modernization.

findings.title: No draft/pending state for agent-proposed writes
findings.description: No draft or pending state exists. The cmdSave_Click handler immediately executes an INSERT into the database with no intermediate review step. All write operations are immediately committed.
findings.gap: No mechanism for an agent to propose a change that a human can review before commitment.
findings.recommendation: Add a status column (DRAFT/CONFIRMED) to enable human-in-the-loop review.

findings.title: No configurable approval gates

findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without disrupting all callers.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent API key management with revocation capability.

findings.title: No Input Validation — Active Injection Vulnerabilities
findings.description: No input validation. SQL injection via string concatenation with partnerId and XML-parsed values. XXE vulnerability via unprotected DocumentBuilderFactory. No schema enforcement or size limits.
findings.gap: Active SQL injection and XXE vulnerabilities. No validation at API boundary.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries (PreparedStatement). Disable external entities. Add XML schema validation and input size limits.

findings.title: No Temporal Metadata
findings.description: No timestamps in database records (no created_at, updated_at, event_time). No freshness signaling in responses.
findings.gap: Cannot determine when data was created or its freshness.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at (UTC) and updated_at columns. Include timestamps in API responses.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Leaked in Error Responses
findings.description: Raw exception messages returned to callers can expose DB connection strings, SQL statements, and partner data. No PII/sensitive-data redaction.
findings.gap: No redaction in error responses. Infrastructure details and potentially PII leaked.
findings.recommendation: Replace raw exception returns with generic error codes. Log full details server-side only.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or Contract Stability
findings.description: No schema versioning. WSDL has no version identifier. No breaking change detection, no contract tests, no CI/CD.
findings.gap: No API versioning or contract stability guarantees. Agent tool bindings break silently.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning and contract tests (Pact) in replacement service.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC. Infrastructure (JBoss AS 5.1, RHEL 6, Oracle 11g) managed manually. No peer review, no drift detection.
findings.gap: No IaC governance. Infrastructure changes manual and unauditable.
findings.recommendation: Define all replacement infrastructure as code (CDK or Terraform).

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD. Manual Ant build with hand-run wsgen/wsimport. No automated testing, no contract tests.
findings.gap: API changes cannot be caught before production.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with API contract testing for replacement service.

findings.title: No Rollback Capability
findings.description: No automated rollback. Manual WAR deployment only. Cannot quickly revert bad deployments.
findings.gap: Recovery from bad deployments is manual and slow.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green or canary deployment with automatic rollback.

findings.title: Zero Test Coverage
findings.description: No automated tests. README states: 'No tests; partner onboarding is a manual SOAP-UI session.'
findings.gap: No automated validation of API behavior.
findings.recommendation: Implement comprehensive API test suites (integration + contract tests) running in CI.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configuration. Oracle 11g with no evidence of TDE or KMS. Partner financial data stored unencrypted.
findings.gap: Data at rest not encrypted. Breach exposes all partner order data.
findings.recommendation: Use KMS-encrypted managed databases (RDS with encryption) in replacement architecture.

findings.title: No Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No draft or pending state. All writes immediately committed. Orders cannot be proposed for human review.
findings.gap: No mechanism for agent-proposed writes to await human confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Add order status lifecycle (PENDING → CONFIRMED) with confirmation endpoint.

findings.title: No Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval gates. No configurable operation-level flags, no approval workflows. All operations execute immediately.
findings.gap: Cannot require human approval for high-risk agent operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement configurable approval gates (e.g., orders above threshold require confirmation).

findings.title: No Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment. Manual SOAP-UI testing only. No safe environment for agent testing.
findings.gap: First agent bug discovered in production.
findings.recommendation: Create containerized staging environment with synthetic test data.

findings.title: Zero Observability — No Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray, no logging framework. Agent-initiated requests completely opaque.
findings.gap: Cannot trace, correlate, or diagnose agent-initiated requests.
findings.recommendation: Implement OpenTelemetry SDK with trace ID propagation and structured JSON logging.

findings.title: No Alerting Configuration
findings.description: No alerting on error rates or latency. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection.
findings.gap: Service degradation affecting agents goes undetected.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms for error rate and p99 latency.

findings.title: Write-Only Interface — No Queryable State
findings.description: No query endpoints. The service is write-only — accepts orders but provides no way to inspect current state.
findings.gap: Agents cannot read before writing. No GET/query endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Add query endpoints (GET /orders/{id}, GET /orders?partnerId=X) in replacement API.

findings.title: No Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No optimistic locking, no version fields, no ETags. Concurrent submitOrder calls create duplicate or conflicting records.
findings.gap: No protection against race conditions from concurrent agent instances.
findings.recommendation: Implement optimistic locking with version columns or unique constraints.

findings.title: No Circuit Breakers or Resilience
findings.description: No circuit breakers, no retry logic, no timeout configuration. Raw JDBC connection with no pooling. Database failures cascade directly to callers.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns. Runaway agent loops cascade through database dependency.
findings.recommendation: Implement connection pooling (HikariCP) and circuit breaker pattern (Resilience4j).

findings.title: No Rate Limiting
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application-level throttling. Agent traffic storms would overwhelm the database.
findings.gap: No protection against runaway agent loops.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with usage plans and throttling. Add WAF rate rules.

findings.title: No Transaction Limits — Unbounded Blast Radius
findings.description: No transaction limits. No maximum records per caller, no spend limits, no bulk operation caps. Agent error blast radius is unbounded.
findings.gap: No configurable limits on agent-initiated actions.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller transaction limits (max orders per hour, max amount per order).

findings.title: No Async Support for 5-7 Hour Batch
findings.description: Batch runs 5-7 hours with no job status API, no polling endpoint, no webhook callback. No way to query progress.
findings.gap: No async patterns for long-running operation.
findings.recommendation: Implement job submission with status polling mechanism.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions Infrastructure
findings.description: No authorization model exists. No IAM policies, no RACF granular profiles, no role definitions. Cannot differentiate access levels.
findings.gap: No scoped permissions. Cannot grant read-only vs full access.
findings.recommendation: Implement role-based access with separate profiles for job submission, data read, and data write.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization. Single monolithic batch with no operation-level permissions. Cannot restrict read vs write vs execute.
findings.gap: No fine-grained RBAC or ABAC. Cannot restrict agent to read-only.
findings.recommendation: Decompose into separate read and write operations with independent authorization.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation or Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation. Shared FTP credential with no per-caller attribution. Cannot distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.gap: No identity context passed through service calls. All actions appear from shared identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement identity-aware job submission capturing and propagating requesting principal.

findings.title: Hardcoded Plaintext Credentials in Source Control
findings.description: FTP credentials hardcoded in plaintext in JCL: username 'payroll', password 'PayR0ll2003!' visible in source. Committed to version control with no rotation capability.
findings.gap: No secrets management. Hardcoded credentials vulnerable to leak via prompt injection or code exposure.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials immediately. Implement Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Replace FTP with SFTP.

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Mechanism
findings.description: No mechanism to suspend or revoke agent identities. No identities exist to suspend. Cannot isolate misbehaving agent without full system shutdown.
findings.gap: No identity suspension capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement revocable service identities with immediate disable capability.

findings.title: No PII Redaction in Logs or Transmission
findings.description: No PII redaction. SSN and bank account data transmitted in plaintext via FTP. No masking in SYSOUT logs. No log scrubbing.
findings.gap: PII unprotected in logs and network transmission.
findings.recommendation: Implement PII redaction in all logging. Replace plaintext FTP with encrypted transfer. Mask SSN in non-essential output.

findings.title: No Input Validation or Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation. Records processed without data type or range checks. No validation for hours, rates, SSN format. Malformed data processed silently.
findings.gap: No validation at any boundary. Incorrect data produces incorrect payroll calculations.
findings.recommendation: Add input validation for employee hours, pay rates, SSN format with structured error reporting.

findings.title: No Temporal Metadata or Freshness Signaling
findings.description: No timestamps in employee records. No freshness signaling. FICA wage base hardcoded at stale 2019 value ($132,900).
findings.gap: No temporal metadata. No mechanism to detect or communicate data staleness.
findings.recommendation: Add temporal metadata fields and automated staleness detection for reference data.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or Breaking Change Detection
findings.description: No schema versioning. Fixed-width 120-byte file format with no version identifier, no documentation, no breaking change detection.
findings.gap: No versioning. Format changes would silently break all consumers.
findings.recommendation: Document file format as versioned schema with format version headers.

findings.title: Zero Automated Test Coverage
findings.description: No automated tests exist. Manual validation in shared QA region only. No regression detection capability.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage. No CI pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Create automated tests for payroll calculation logic and end-to-end batch verification.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest for Sensitive Data
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Employee master file containing SSN and bank accounts stored unencrypted on z/OS datasets.
findings.gap: Sensitive PII and financial data unencrypted at rest.
findings.recommendation: Enable dataset encryption for PII-containing files. Apply KMS-equivalent key management.

findings.title: No Draft/Pending State for Review
findings.description: No draft or pending state. Output committed and transmitted immediately upon batch completion. No reviewable intermediate state.
findings.gap: All write operations immediately committed. No human review gate.
findings.recommendation: Implement PENDING state between payroll computation and output transmission.

findings.title: No Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval gates. Batch runs unconditionally to completion once triggered with no human approval step.
findings.gap: Cannot require human approval for high-value operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement threshold-based approval gates for high-value payroll runs.

findings.title: Shared QA Region Only — No Isolated Sandbox
findings.description: Only a shared QA region exists for testing. No isolated sandbox with synthetic data for agent testing.
findings.gap: No production-equivalent staging with data isolation.
findings.recommendation: Establish isolated staging environment with synthetic payroll data.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No tracing or structured logging. Unstructured JCL SYSOUT only. Cannot trace agent-triggered executions end-to-end.
findings.gap: No tracing infrastructure. No correlation IDs.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured logging with unique execution IDs and trace context propagation.

findings.title: No Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No concurrency controls. DISP=SHR allows concurrent reads with no locking. Concurrent execution would produce duplicate/corrupt output.
findings.gap: No optimistic locking, no mutex, no duplicate run detection.
findings.recommendation: Implement execution-level mutex and run-sequence identifier.

findings.title: No Circuit Breakers or Resilience Patterns
findings.description: No circuit breakers, retry logic, or timeout configurations. FTP step to EC2 gateway has no error handling — failures cascade without protection.
findings.gap: No resilience for external FTP dependency.
findings.recommendation: Add retry logic with exponential backoff and timeout for FTP step.

findings.title: No Blast Radius or Transaction Limits
findings.description: No transaction limits. Batch processes ALL employees without configurable scope. Single execution affects entire employee population with no per-run limits.
findings.gap: No blast radius limits. No configurable transaction scope per identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement configurable transaction limits — maximum records per run, pay-period scope validation.

findings.title: No Queryable Current State
findings.description: No queryable state API. Employee data accessible only via COBOL I/O on mainframe. Cannot inspect state before acting.
findings.gap: No read-before-write capability. No external query interface.
findings.recommendation: Expose queryable state layer for employee and job status data.

findings.title: No machine-readable API specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, Smithy model, or any machine-readable API specification exists. The API contract is defined only implicitly in pricing.cpp source code.
findings.gap: Agent tool generation requires manual work. No automated tool binding, no client SDK generation, no contract validation.
findings.recommendation: Create an openapi.yaml file describing the /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi endpoint with query parameters (sku, qty) and response schema.

findings.title: No structured error responses
findings.description: All responses return HTTP 200 with HTML regardless of outcome. When a SKU is not found, the response shows Unit: $0.00 with no error differentiation. No structured error codes, no HTTP 4xx/5xx, no machine-readable error body.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish between SKU not found (terminal), rules file unavailable (retriable), and success — all return HTTP 200 with HTML.
findings.recommendation: Return appropriate HTTP status codes (404 for unknown SKU, 500 for file read failure) with a JSON error body containing error code, message, and retryable boolean.

findings.title: No scoped permissions model
findings.description: No authorization model exists. The application has no concept of permissions, roles, or access scopes. All callers have identical unrestricted access to all pricing data.
findings.gap: No mechanism to scope agent permissions to specific SKUs, price tiers, or operations.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an API Gateway layer with scoped API keys or OAuth2 scopes that allow differentiating caller access levels.

findings.title: No action-level authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The application has a single action (lookup price) with no granularity. No authorization infrastructure to support future write operations or differentiated access.
findings.gap: No ABAC, RBAC, or fine-grained permission model. Cannot enforce action-level access control.
findings.recommendation: When adding authentication (AUTH-Q1), implement role-based access with at least read and admin scopes.

findings.title: No immutable audit logging
findings.description: No audit logging is configured. The application produces no logs of its own. No CloudTrail, CloudWatch, or structured logging is defined anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: No immutable audit trail for API calls. Cannot determine which agent accessed which pricing data and when.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with access logging to CloudWatch Logs. Enable CloudTrail for API Gateway events. Configure log retention with S3 object lock for immutability.

findings.title: No input validation — buffer overflow vulnerabilities
findings.description: The application has NO input validation. The parse_query function uses strcpy without bounds checking — an attacker-controlled SKU parameter can overflow the 64-byte sku buffer. The qty parameter is parsed with atoi which accepts arbitrary strings without validation.
findings.gap: Agents sending malformed payloads (oversized SKU strings, non-numeric qty values) cause undefined behavior including buffer overflows. No structured rejection signals exist for self-correction.
findings.recommendation: Replace strcpy with strncpy with bounds checking. Validate SKU length and qty range. Return structured error responses for invalid input. Consider rewriting in a memory-safe language.

findings.title: No schema versioning or API contracts
findings.description: No API versioning, no schema files, no contract documentation, no changelog, no breaking change detection. The CGI URL has no version prefix. No consumer-driven contract tests exist.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings will break silently if the response format or query parameters change. No mechanism to detect or communicate breaking changes.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL versioning (e.g., /v1/pricing), document the API contract in an OpenAPI spec, and add contract validation to CI.

findings.title: No IaC governance for integration surface
findings.description: No IaC defines the integration surface (API gateways, IAM roles, secrets, networking). Kubernetes manifests exist for the deployment itself, but no Terraform, CloudFormation, or CDK defines the surrounding infrastructure.
findings.gap: The agent-facing integration surface is not defined as code. Changes are manual and unauditable.
findings.recommendation: Define the full integration surface in IaC (Terraform or CDK): API Gateway, IAM roles, WAF rules, CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline or contract testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild configuration. The Makefile deploys via scp to a production server. No automated testing or contract validation.
findings.gap: API contract changes cannot be caught before agents are affected. No automated deployment pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Create a CI pipeline that builds the Docker image, runs health checks, and validates the API contract.

findings.title: Limited rollback capability
findings.description: Kubernetes deployment provides native rollback via kubectl rollout undo. However, there is no automated rollback trigger, no canary deployment, no progressive delivery configuration.
findings.gap: Rollback exists via Kubernetes native mechanism but is manual with no automated triggers.
findings.recommendation: Configure rollback triggers based on readiness probe failures. Consider Argo Rollouts for automated canary analysis.

findings.title: No staging or sandbox environment
findings.description: No staging environment. Dockerfile provides local build with a single sample SKU (SAMPLE-SKU|9.99), not production-equivalent data. No environment-specific configurations.
findings.gap: Cannot test agents against realistic pricing data in a safe environment before production deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create a staging namespace with production-equivalent pricing rules. Add Kustomize environment overlay with realistic sample data.

findings.title: No distributed tracing or structured logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs. The CGI binary writes HTML to stdout and produces no logs. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray instrumentation, no JSON log output.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated requests cannot be traced through the system. Failures are not debuggable.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging (JSON to stderr) with request_id correlation. Instrument with OpenTelemetry or X-Ray for trace propagation.

findings.title: No alerting on error rates or latency
findings.description: No alerting is configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration. Only Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes exist.
findings.gap: Target system degradation goes undetected until agents fail. No error rate or latency thresholds configured.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms for HTTP 5xx error rate and p99 latency on the pricing endpoint.

findings.title: No rate limiting or throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting exists at any layer. The CGI endpoint processes every request without throttling. No API Gateway throttling, no WAF rules, no application-level rate limiting middleware.
findings.gap: No protection against traffic storms from agent bugs or misconfigured retry loops. The service has only 2 replicas with 500m CPU limit — easily exhaustible.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway or ingress controller with throttle configuration (e.g., 100 requests/second per caller). Alternatively, add WAF rate-based rules.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, or machine-readable specification found. API endpoints only discoverable by reading source code.
findings.gap: Agent frameworks cannot auto-generate tool definitions from this API.
findings.recommendation: Create an openapi.yaml specification documenting both endpoints with request/response schemas.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses are minimal unstructured objects: { error: 'db error' }, { error: 'invalid api key' }. No error codes, no retryable indicators.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors. All failures look the same.
findings.recommendation: Implement consistent error format with error_code, message, and retryable fields.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: A single shared API key grants identical access to all callers. No mechanism to differentiate access levels — all requests with the valid key can access both GET /rates and POST /quote equally.
findings.gap: No scoped permission model exists. Cannot grant an agent read-only access to /rates without also granting access to /quote.
findings.recommendation: Introduce API Gateway with usage plans that scope each caller to specific endpoints and methods.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The API key middleware applies uniformly — any valid key holder can call any endpoint with any HTTP method.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to read operations (GET) while blocking computation (POST) at the authorization layer.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level authorization — either at API Gateway or as application middleware mapping caller identity to allowed HTTP methods and paths.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: API key hardcoded in source: var API_KEY = 'ship-2013-abc123-static'. MongoDB URL hardcoded: var MONGO_URL = 'mongodb://10.0.8.20:27017/shipping'. No secrets management system is used.
findings.gap: Credentials embedded in source code. No rotation capability. Exposure risk via repository access.
findings.recommendation: Refactor application to read credentials from environment variables. Store in AWS Secrets Manager with rotation. K8s deployment already references a Secret — connect the application to consume it.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. Only output is console.log('Shipping API listening on 8080'). No request logging, no principal attribution, no immutable storage.
findings.gap: Zero audit trail for API access. Cannot determine who accessed what, when.
findings.recommendation: Add structured request logging middleware with caller attribution. Ship to CloudWatch Logs with retention policy. Configure S3 log archival with Object Lock for immutability.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: Single shared API key means no per-agent suspension capability. Revoking access affects all consumers simultaneously.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without disrupting all service consumers.
findings.recommendation: Resolve AUTH-Q1 first (per-caller identity), which naturally enables per-identity suspension via API Gateway key deletion.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: GET /rates supports origin/dest filtering but has no pagination, sorting, or result size limits. All matching documents returned as full array.
findings.gap: Unbounded result sets possible from broad queries. Agent queries may exhaust LLM context.
findings.recommendation: Add limit/offset parameters with default (100) and maximum (1000) limits.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation. Query params passed directly to MongoDB filter without sanitization. POST /quote reads weight/zone without type checking. NoSQL injection risk present.
findings.gap: Malformed agent inputs accepted without rejection or structured error feedback.
findings.recommendation: Add validation library (joi/express-validator). Sanitize MongoDB query inputs. Return structured validation errors.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: No temporal metadata in API responses. No timestamps, no Cache-Control headers, no data freshness signaling.
findings.gap: Agents cannot determine when shipping rates were last updated or if data is stale.
findings.recommendation: Add updated_at timestamps to rate documents. Return Cache-Control and Last-Modified headers.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No API versioning (no /v1/ prefix, no Accept-Version header). No schema documentation, no changelog, no breaking change detection, no contract tests.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings break silently if API response format changes.
findings.recommendation: Add URL-based versioning (/v1/rates). Document response schemas. Add contract tests.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance
findings.description: K8s manifests provide partial IaC (namespace, configmap, deployment, service). No API Gateway, IAM, or networking defined as code. No PR review requirements or drift detection.
findings.gap: Agent-facing integration surface not fully governed as code.
findings.recommendation: Adopt GitOps for K8s manifests. Define API Gateway and IAM as Terraform/CDK.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or buildspec.yml. No automated testing or contract testing.
findings.gap: API breaking changes cannot be caught before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create CI pipeline with Docker build and API contract tests.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No rollback strategy configured. K8s Deployment uses :latest tag with default RollingUpdate. No blue/green, canary, or automated rollback.
findings.gap: Cannot reliably roll back to previous version if change breaks agent APIs.
findings.recommendation: Pin image tags to specific versions. Configure automated rollback on failed health checks.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: Zero automated tests. No test framework, no test files, no test dependencies in package.json.
findings.gap: No verification of API behavior for agent consumption.
findings.recommendation: Add jest + supertest integration tests for both endpoints covering valid/invalid inputs and error responses.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: MongoDB connection uses plaintext (no TLS). No encryption-at-rest configuration. No KMS references. MongoDB has no authentication.
findings.gap: Data at rest and in transit is unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Enable MongoDB TLS. Enable encryption at rest. Consider migration to Amazon DocumentDB.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration. No docker-compose, no seed data scripts, no environment-specific configs.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior without affecting production.
findings.recommendation: Create docker-compose.yml with MongoDB and seed data for local testing.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs. Only a single console.log startup message.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated requests are completely opaque. Cannot diagnose failures.
findings.recommendation: Add pino (structured JSON logger) with request-id middleware. Instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring integration, no SLO-based alerting.
findings.gap: Service degradation undetectable until agents report failures.
findings.recommendation: Deploy CloudWatch Container Insights. Configure alarms on 5xx error rate and p99 latency.

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanisms exist. The system performs no write operations — GET reads from MongoDB, POST computes a value. No saga patterns or undo endpoints.
findings.gap: No transactional framework exists. Low practical impact given read-only operations.
findings.recommendation: Lower priority given no write operations. Implement saga patterns if write endpoints are added.

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: No circuit breakers, retry logic, or timeout configurations for MongoDB dependency. New connection opened per request with no pooling or timeout.
findings.gap: MongoDB failures cascade to all callers with no protection or graceful degradation.
findings.recommendation: Implement MongoDB connection pooling, add timeouts, and introduce circuit breaker pattern (opossum library).

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No middleware, no API Gateway, no WAF rules. Express app has no protection against traffic storms.
findings.gap: No protection against agent-driven traffic storms. A runaway agent loop could overwhelm the service.
findings.recommendation: Add express-rate-limit middleware immediately. Deploy API Gateway or NGINX Ingress with throttling for production.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or Smithy model exists. The API surface is defined only implicitly through Rails controller code.
findings.gap: No machine-readable spec. Agent tool definitions require manual authoring from code inspection.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI 3.0 specification documenting orders endpoints, request/response schemas, and error codes.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Errors render HTML forms. No JSON error bodies, no error codes, no retryable indicators. Agents cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.gap: No structured error response format for machine consumption.
findings.recommendation: Implement consistent JSON error format with error code, message, and retryable boolean across all endpoints.

findings.title: No Asynchronous Operation Support
findings.description: Payment SOAP call is synchronous within the HTTP request cycle. No background jobs, no async/polling pattern, no job status API.
findings.gap: Long-running payment operations block HTTP requests with no async alternative.
findings.recommendation: Move payment processing to async workflow with job status polling endpoint.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: No authorization model exists. All callers have identical unrestricted access to all endpoints and data.
findings.gap: No permission scoping mechanism. Cannot differentiate access levels.
findings.recommendation: Implement RBAC with scoped roles for agent callers after establishing authentication.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization. Any caller can perform any action (read, create, charge payment).
findings.gap: Cannot restrict agent to read-only access within the same resource type.
findings.recommendation: Implement fine-grained RBAC with action-level permissions.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation. No JWT parsing, no OAuth2 token exchange, no on-behalf-of flows.
findings.gap: Cannot distinguish agent-as-self from agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.recommendation: Implement JWT-based identity propagation after establishing machine identity.

findings.title: Credentials in Source Control
findings.description: Live payment gateway credentials (merchant_id, api_password) stored in plaintext in version-controlled config/payment.yml.
findings.gap: Credentials in source control. No secrets management. No rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Rotate credentials immediately. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation.

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: No identity management exists. No mechanism to suspend or revoke agent access without full application shutdown.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate misbehaving agent without taking down entire application.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key-based auth with immediate revocation capability.

findings.title: No Pagination or Result Size Limits
findings.description: Index action returns all matching orders with no pagination, no LIMIT clause, no cursor support. Unbounded result sets.
findings.gap: No pagination. Agent queries could return unbounded result sets exceeding context windows.
findings.recommendation: Implement pagination with limit/offset or cursor-based navigation and result size caps.

findings.title: No Input Validation — SQL Injection and Mass Assignment
findings.description: No input validation. SQL injection via direct string interpolation in find_by_sql. Mass assignment via Order.new(params[:order]) with no attr_accessible.
findings.gap: No validation at any layer. SQL injection and mass assignment vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Fix SQL injection with parameterized queries. Add attr_accessible. Implement request validation.

findings.title: Minimal Temporal Metadata
findings.description: created_at field exists (referenced in ORDER BY). No updated_at evidence, no timezone normalization, no freshness signaling to callers.
findings.gap: Minimal temporal metadata. No update tracking or freshness signaling.
findings.recommendation: Ensure created_at/updated_at exposed in responses. Add Cache-Control headers.

findings.title: No PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: System processes credit card numbers. Rails 2.3 default logging logs request parameters including card data. No filter_parameter_logging, no PII masking.
findings.gap: No PII redaction. Credit card numbers likely appear in default Rails request logs.
findings.recommendation: Add filter_parameter_logging for sensitive fields. Implement log scrubbing middleware.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No versioned URLs, no Accept-Version headers, no changelog, no database migrations, no breaking change detection, no contract tests.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings could break silently on any deployment.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-based API versioning and breaking change detection in CI.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC. Manual EC2 management via Capistrano 2 to fixed hosts. No Terraform, CloudFormation, or CDK.
findings.gap: No infrastructure governance. Manual error-prone changes. No drift detection.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure as IaC using Terraform or CloudFormation with PR-based review.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Manual Capistrano deployment. No contract testing, no automated testing in pipeline.
findings.gap: No automated testing or contract validation. Changes deployed without verification.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with automated testing and API contract validation.

findings.title: Limited Rollback Capability
findings.description: Capistrano 2 provides basic code rollback. No automated triggers, no database rollback, no traffic shifting, no canary deployments.
findings.gap: Rollback limited to Capistrano code revert. No automated rollback triggers.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green deployment with automated rollback triggers on error rate metrics.

findings.title: No API Test Coverage
findings.description: Stale Test::Unit suite that no longer runs. No test files present. No API tests, integration tests, or contract tests.
findings.gap: No working test coverage. Agent-facing behavior changes unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Create automated API test suite covering order operations. Run in CI.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: MySQL 5.1 on EC2 with no encryption at rest. Credit card data stored unencrypted. No KMS, no encrypted EBS volumes.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for PCI-regulated card data.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS with KMS encryption at rest. Encrypt EBS volumes.

findings.title: No Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No draft or pending state. Orders immediately committed and payment charged in single request with no intermediate review.
findings.gap: No reviewable intermediate state for agent-proposed writes.
findings.recommendation: Add PENDING status to order lifecycle before payment processing.

findings.title: No Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval gates. All operations execute immediately without oversight. Cannot require human confirmation for high-risk operations.
findings.gap: No configurable approval gates for high-risk agent-initiated operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement configurable approval gates by operation type and amount threshold.

findings.title: No Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No staging environment documented. Payment gateway configured for live mode only. No docker-compose, no seed data.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior. First bug discovery in production.
findings.recommendation: Create staging environment with payment test mode and seed data.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation. No structured logging — Rails 2.3 uses unstructured text logs. No correlation IDs.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated request failures not debuggable.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON logging with correlation IDs and distributed tracing.

findings.title: No Alerting on Error Rates or Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no monitoring.
findings.gap: System degradation undetectable until agent failures cascade.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency for all endpoints.

findings.title: SQL-Injection Vulnerable Query Interface
findings.description: Index action queries by status via SQL injection-vulnerable code. Show returns individual order. Query interface is rudimentary and unsafe.
findings.gap: Query interface uses direct string interpolation in SQL. Unsafe for agent consumption.
findings.recommendation: Replace SQL injection-vulnerable query with parameterized queries. Add safe filter and pagination.

findings.title: No Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No optimistic locking, no version fields, no ETags, no conditional writes. Concurrent agent instances could cause race conditions.
findings.gap: No concurrency controls. Concurrent agent writes could corrupt state.
findings.recommendation: Add optimistic locking (version column) and idempotency keys.

findings.title: No Circuit Breakers for External Dependencies
findings.description: External SOAP payment gateway call has no circuit breaker, no retry logic, no timeout configuration. Gateway failures cascade to all callers.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns for external dependency calls.
findings.recommendation: Implement circuit breaker with configurable timeout, retry with exponential backoff, and fallback behavior.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF rate rules, no application middleware. Mongrel behind Apache with no throttling.
findings.gap: Runaway agent loops can overwhelm the application and downstream payment gateway.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with per-caller throttling configuration.

findings.title: No Blast Radius or Transaction Limits
findings.description: No transaction limits. No per-caller caps, no maximum spend limits, no bulk operation size constraints. Agent error could trigger unlimited payment charges.
findings.gap: No blast radius caps. Unbounded agent-initiated operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller transaction limits (max orders/hour, max charge/session).

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or machine-readable specification exists.
findings.gap: Complete absence of machine-readable specifications.
findings.recommendation: Generate OpenAPI spec when building the new REST API layer.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No structured error handling. customErrors disabled exposes raw stack traces. No error codes or retryable indicators.
findings.gap: No error codes, no machine-readable error bodies.
findings.recommendation: Implement consistent structured JSON error responses in the new API layer.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: Single database user for all operations. No role-based access control differentiation. All authenticated users share identical permissions.
findings.gap: No mechanism to scope down agent access per capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement role-based authorization with separate read/write database roles.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization. All authenticated users can read and write equally with no permission differentiation.
findings.gap: No fine-grained RBAC or ABAC policies.
findings.recommendation: Implement action-level authorization (separate read vs write permissions).

findings.title: No Identity Propagation or Delegation
